name: showreel-49-scrollbar
style: Black look (rule 19) with a lime accent: near-black, no frame or glow, one accent word, whole frame, calm. E30 wiggle family, scroll-driven: a feed scrolls on every flick; BEFORE a script moves the bar in late steps (hatched gap + white tick show where it should be), JS CALLS climbs; AFTER animation-timeline: scroll() locks the bar to the scroll, JS CALLS stays 0

voice.text: Why is your scroll bar late? A script catches every scroll, so the bar can lag behind the page. The fix: animation timeline scroll. Now the scroll itself drives the bar, so no code runs, and nothing is late.

caption:
Why is your scroll bar late? 📏 The page scrolls, the bar trails behind it.

The usual way: a script listens to every scroll event and then moves the bar. That is code running on each scroll, and the bar can lag behind the page. The fix: tie the animation to the scroll itself with animation-timeline: scroll(); (put it after the animation shorthand). Then no script runs: watch JS CALLS climb before the fix and stay at 0 after.

MDN: animation-timeline specifies the timeline that controls a CSS animation, and scroll() is an anonymous scroll progress timeline. Support: Chrome 115, Firefox 159, Safari 26 (MDN browser compatibility).

Save it for your next reading progress bar, or send it to whoever still has a scroll listener for this.

sources.note: MDN animation-timeline (read 27 Nov 2026): the property specifies the timeline used to control the progress of a CSS animation; scroll() is an anonymous scroll progress timeline
MDN BCD css.properties.animation-timeline (read 27 Nov 2026): Chrome 115, Firefox 159, Safari 26
